Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Is a logical link diagram enough to assess physical risk?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It omits pitch, layer transitions, materials, and return-path geometry.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A chiplet-to-chiplet signal may cross bumps, RDL or interposer wiring, another bump field, and return paths. Trace the visual in order: die pad; package route; destination pad. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Trace one data lane from a compute chiplet to memory and mark each physical interface where loss or failure can occur.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R3: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 22: Interconnects | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch22_2D-3D.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Trace one data lane from a compute chiplet to memory and mark each physical interface where loss or failure can occur. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Bump pitch and pad arrangement determine whether inner rows can reach legal routing channels. Trace the visual in order: bump grid; via escape; routing layer. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Sketch an inner bump row. Name one legal via route and one keep-out before asserting that the link is feasible.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
